item.title: Materials beyond silicon photonics emerge for scalable quantum photonic systems
item.description: The shift beyond silicon photonics is an expansion of the photonic materials toolkit. While silicon remains valuable for electronic-photonic integration and certain passive functions, scalable quantum photonic systems demand materials engineered specifically for quantum performance.

item.description: Let us know if the recent U.S. Supreme Court decision will prompt your company to pursue a refund of tariffs paid.

item.title: Thermoelectric coolers prevent thermal drift within compact optical systems
item.description: Thermoelectric coolers provide precision temperature control for lasers, detectors, and integrated photonics—where addressing thermal drift at the device level is essential.

item.title: Gamechanger: A polymer infrared thermal imaging lens
item.description: Traditional lenses made of germanium tend to cost hundreds or thousands of dollars and can’t be repaired when damaged—but a lower-cost sulfur polymer lens option is about to become a gamechanger for infrared (IR) thermal imaging cameras because it can be mass produced, repaired, and recycled.

item.title: Optical cavity for each atom within a quantum computer?
item.description: Microlenses inside optical cavities allow physicists to tightly focus light onto single atoms in a way that’s both efficient and massively parallel—and it looks promising for building faster distributed quantum computers.

item.title: Silicon photonics at scale will power AI data centers
item.description: Silicon photonics is system‑defining for artificial intelligence (AI) data center technology—and the ability to align design, manufacturing, and supply into a repeatable global engine is a powerful position.
